questions.question: A single support agent with ten tools and a huge prompt keeps making mistakes. What does the Agents SDK suggest?
options: Add more instructions to the same prompt
Split it into a triage agent and specialists, and hand off between them
Remove all tools
Use a smaller model
questions.explanation: Handoffs let each specialist keep a focused prompt and toolset while the conversation moves between them.

questions.question: How does the model trigger a handoff?
options: By writing 'HANDOFF' in its reply
By calling a tool named transfer_to_<agent>; the Runner switches the active agent
The Runner picks an agent at random
By returning a special HTTP status
questions.explanation: Handoffs are exposed as tools. The 'result' of calling one is that the next turn runs with the target agent's instructions and tools.

questions.question: After a handoff, what does the specialist agent see?
options: Only the last user message
Its own instructions plus the full conversation history so far
Nothing until the user writes again
The triage agent's instructions
questions.explanation: The history carries over; the system instructions and tools switch to the new agent's.

questions.question: In the real SDK, input guardrails default to run_in_parallel=True. What does that mean when one trips?
options: No model call ever happens
The first model call may already have started (and cost money) before the run is aborted
The guardrail is skipped
The run continues and ignores the tripwire
questions.explanation: Parallel guardrails save latency on good input. Set run_in_parallel=False when the check must complete before any model call.

questions.question: Your output_type is a @dataclass and the SDK keeps raising 'Invalid JSON when parsing model output' on valid-looking JSON. What's a likely fix?
options: Increase max_turns
Use a Pydantic BaseModel; the SDK wraps non-BaseModel types under a 'response' key
Disable guardrails
Switch to plain text output
questions.explanation: In SDK 0.25.0 a dataclass output type is wrapped, so the expected JSON is {'response': {...}}. A BaseModel is used as the schema directly.

questions.question: When should a specialist be an agent-as-tool rather than a handoff?
options: When the specialist should take over the conversation
When the calling agent should stay in charge and use the specialist's result as one input
Never; handoffs are always better
When there's only one agent
questions.explanation: Handoffs transfer control; agents-as-tools return a result to the caller, which is the orchestrator–worker shape.
